fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the overnight rate US banks lend at. Its decisions price dollar borrowing worldwide, from American mortgages to emerging-market debt.
fomc-2026-12.recent: It is the first meeting since Democrats took the Senate and with it the confirmation of every future Fed governor, the lever a president uses to seat members picked to push rates down. Warsh arrives after a hold TD Securities expected to draw 3 dissents, his muddled messaging already reviving doubts about Fed credibility.

g20-2026-miami.standing: The annual meeting of leaders of the world's largest economies, hosted by the member holding the rotating presidency. Its members produce about 85% of global output, and its communiqué sets shared lines on trade and debt.
g20-2026-miami.recent: Atlanta's foreign ministers' meeting ended with no group photo, after Europeans refused to stand beside Lavrov, and no joint statement. The EU's Kallas said hosting Putin risks normalising war crimes; Rubio defended Russia's seat and floated a Black Sea ceasefire. The summit tests whether the US presidency can keep both in the room.

ecb-2026-12.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which meets eight times a year to set interest rates for the countries sharing the euro. Its deposit rate drives borrowing costs for some 350 million people, and the euro moves with it.
ecb-2026-12.recent: Eurozone inflation hit 4% in October on fossil-fuel prices from the Iran war. The Bundesbank's Nagel has backed a December hike and Panetta says more may be needed, even as firms report tighter credit. Governments are meanwhile nominating a successor to Lagarde, who leaves on 7 February 2027.

boe-2026-12.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who vote eight times a year on Bank Rate. Their decision sets the price of UK mortgages and business loans, and sterling and gilt yields move with it.
boe-2026-12.recent: This meeting follows the Bank's first hike since 2023, made alongside a forecast that inflation will peak at 4.9% as the Iran war's energy shock feeds through. Bailey has said a second hike is more likely than not if the war goes on, so the decision turns on the conflict, and so does what UK mortgage holders on variable rates pay.

boj-2026-12.standing: The Bank of Japan's policy board, which meets eight times a year to set the country's short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen and the yield on Japanese government debt, and reach borrowers far beyond Japan.
boj-2026-12.recent: Japan's argument has turned to whether its inflation is now driven by wages rather than a weak yen, and that distinction is what this decision rests on. It arrives with markets fully pricing a December Fed rate hike, which widens the rate gap that has weighed on the yen, just as foreign issuers sold a record $16 billion of yen bonds.

fred-us-jobs-report-2026-11-06.standing: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly employment report, released on the first Friday of most months, counting jobs added, the unemployment rate and wage growth. Treasury yields, the dollar and Fed rate bets reprice within minutes.
fred-us-jobs-report-2026-11-06.recent: The release lands in the same week as the U.S. midterms, so the first official read on hiring after the vote arrives while the result is still being absorbed. It settles how many jobs employers added last month and where unemployment stands.

fred-us-cpi-2026-11-10.standing: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly count of what US households pay for a basket of goods and services. It drives Social Security's yearly raise and inflation-linked Treasury payouts, and bond markets reprice on it within minutes.
fred-us-cpi-2026-11-10.recent: The Fed held rates last month despite intensifying inflation, and Warsh's muddled messaging since has revived doubts about its credibility. This is the first monthly reading since that hold, and it gives the committee its clearest evidence of whether prices kept climbing before it meets again in December.

fred-us-ppi-2026-11-13.standing: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly Producer Price Index, which measures what US businesses receive for goods and services before they reach shoppers. It is an early read on cost pressure that feeds into consumer prices and Fed thinking.
fred-us-ppi-2026-11-13.recent: The US PPI release settles whether price pressure at the wholesale level is building or easing before it reaches shop shelves.
